title: Whole Grilled Tilapia with Grains of Paradise
author: Zoe Adjei
desc: Two tablespoons of ground grains of paradise and two green kpakpo shito, marinated an hour or preferably overnight, grilled twenty-five minutes.
longDesc: The other documented grilled tilapia, and it goes much further in both directions than the charcoal version — a longer marinade and a longer cook. Two fresh tilapia take a grated white onion, rapeseed oil, five centimetres of ginger, a garlic clove, two deseeded green kpakpo shito chillies, the juice of a lime and two full tablespoons of ground grains of paradise, plus chilli flakes and ground hot pepper. An hour minimum, preferably overnight. Then medium-high for twenty-five minutes, turning and basting halfway, until browned and cooked through.
ingredients: 2 fresh tilapia, scaled, gutted and washed
2 green kpakpo shito chillies, deseeded and diced
Salt and black pepper, to taste
steps: Combine the grated onion, oil, ginger, garlic, kpakpo shito, lime juice, grains of paradise, chilli flakes, ground hot pepper, salt and black pepper.
Coat the tilapia inside and out.
Marinate at least 1 hour, preferably overnight.
Grill 25 minutes, adding 3 to 5 minutes for larger fish, turning and basting halfway.
Cook until browned and cooked through.
chefTips: Two tablespoons of ground grains of paradise for two fish is a lot and it is the signature of this recipe. Grains of paradise are peppery and faintly floral and nothing substitutes well.
Overnight is better than the one-hour minimum, by her own framing. With lime juice in the marinade an hour is already doing work.
Turn and baste ONCE, halfway. Twenty-five minutes is a long grill and the basting is what keeps it from drying.
Browned and cooked through is the cue. Twenty-five minutes for a whole tilapia at medium-high is considerably longer than the other documented version's fifteen.
Green kpakpo shito deseeded, which keeps the aroma and loses some heat. Two per fish is generous.
A note on the source: its introduction calls this baked tilapia while the method grills it. The method is what to follow.
If you want the shorter, hotter charcoal treatment, that is GHA094 — fifteen minutes marinating and fifteen minutes cooking.
commonMistakes: Substituting black pepper for grains of paradise.
Following the introduction's baking instruction rather than the method's grill.
sources: Adapted from a whole grilled tilapia recipe on finedininglovers.com, dated 25 May 2021. BYLINE FLAG: the page byline is 'Fine Dining Lovers Editorial Staff' — a site editorial byline, NOT Zoe Adjonyoh. The source credit is to Zoe's Ghana Kitchen, with photography by Nassima Rothacker. Both credits are recorded: the recipe is Adjonyoh's, the page is the site's. Quantities confirmed across two fetches (TWO-PASS).
YIELD: one fetch showed '2 servings (2 whole tilapia)' and the other gave no serves line. The two servings above comes from the first and is flagged as unverified. Total time printed: 1H 55MIN.

Ingredients exactly as printed: 2 fresh tilapia, scaled, gutted and washed; 1 white onion, grated; 1 tablespoon rapeseed oil; 5cm fresh root ginger, grated; 1 garlic clove, finely chopped; 2 green kpakpo shito chillies, deseeded and diced; Juice of 1 lime; 2 tablespoons ground grains of paradise; ½ teaspoon dried chilli flakes; ½ teaspoon ground hot pepper; Salt and black pepper to taste; Lime wedges for serving.
Method as printed: marinate at least 1 hour, 'preferably overnight'; grill medium-high '25 minutes (add 3–5 minutes for larger fish), turning and basting halfway, until browned and cooked through'.

AN INTERNAL CONTRADICTION, flagged and NOT corrected: the introduction on one fetch says 'whole baked tilapia' while the method describes a GRILL. The method is followed above and the discrepancy is recorded.

THE DISAGREEMENT WITH THE OTHER DOCUMENTED GRILLED TILAPIA, unreconciled: 1 hour to overnight marinade and 25 minutes grilling here, against 5-15 minutes marinating and 10-15 minutes over burnt-down charcoal at GHA094. Also note this version uses TWO TABLESPOONS of ground grains of paradise where the other uses none at all. Two quite different fish.
ON GRAINS OF PARADISE: Aframomum melegueta, also called guinea pepper or melegueta pepper, a West African spice in the ginger family. It is the same spice the shito at GHA051 calls 'guinea peppers'.
ON KPAKPO SHITO: the small round Ghanaian chilli, aromatic and moderately hot. Deseeding it, as here, keeps the aroma and reduces the heat.
reheating: Briefly under a hot grill, or eat cold.
healthBenefits: Tilapia is lean, high in protein and low in mercury.
Grains of paradise carry documented antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory compounds.
Lime juice adds vitamin C and helps the marinade penetrate.
Only a tablespoon of oil for two whole fish.
culturalNote: Grains of paradise were once traded north across the Sahara and into medieval Europe as a pepper substitute, and a West African cook using two tablespoons of them on a grilled fish is reaching for something far older than the chilli alongside it. The spice is native to this coast and the dish is the better for it.
